name: Monport GM Pro 60W MOPA
tagline: Integrated 60W JPT MOPA with autofocus: colour marking plus real engraving depth
tldr: The GM Pro 60W MOPA is the most powerful version of Monport's integrated fiber: a 60W JPT MOPA source with 2 mJ of pulse energy, adjustable 2–500 ns pulse, one-touch autofocus and a 175 × 175 mm field. It covers colour marking and deeper engraving (0.10 mm listed per pass) in one compact machine. $3,598 on Monport's store in October 2026, about $670 less than the split GT 60W MOPA with autofocus.
mainObjective: Colour marking, deep engraving and relief on a compact one-piece MOPA

priceRange.note: Official Monport store, Oct 2026: $3,598 machine only, $3,748 with rotary axis, $3,798 with LightBurn Pro; a manual-focus GM 60W MOPA sells for $3,500

engraveExample.description: Filled logo on stainless steel plate

cutExample.description: Not a sheet cutter: thin metal only, in many passes

cannot: Clear glass or acrylic marking (needs UV or CO₂)
Parts larger than the 175 × 175 mm field without repositioning

pros: 2 mJ pulse energy with full MOPA pulse control: colour work and deep engraving from one machine
About $670 less than Monport's split GT 60W MOPA with autofocus ($4,270, Monport store, Oct 2026)
175 × 175 mm field, autofocus and electric lift in a 40 × 33 cm footprint
cons: Only $98 more than the manual-focus GM 60W MOPA: check which version is in the cart
400 mm maximum Z height, against 550 mm on the split GT series
Open galvo and Class 4 beam: an enclosure or strict eye protection is required

faq.question: What is the difference between the GM Pro 60W MOPA and the GM 60W MOPA?
faq.answer: The Pro version has one-touch autofocus and an electric lift; the GM 60W MOPA, listed on the same page at $3,500 in October 2026, is set by hand. For $98 more, the autofocus version is the easier daily machine.

faq.question: GM Pro 60W MOPA or GPro Vision 60W MOPA?
faq.answer: Both use a 60W MOPA source and a 175 × 175 mm field. The GPro Vision is a split fiber with a 16 MP positioning camera at $5,299; the GM Pro 60W MOPA is a one-piece machine without camera at $3,598 (October 2026). Pay for the camera only if you place artwork on many irregular finished parts.

faq.question: Can the GM Pro 60W MOPA cut metal?
faq.answer: Thin sheet, in many passes. With 2 mJ of pulse energy it is the strongest tier of the line for cut-outs and deep relief, but it remains a marking laser with a 175 × 175 mm field.

standoutFeatures.title: Colour and depth in one machine
standoutFeatures.body: 2 mJ of pulse energy and a 2–500 ns adjustable pulse: oxide colours on stainless steel, black marks on aluminum and deep relief on the same compact chassis.

standoutFeatures.title: MOPA 60W under $3,600
standoutFeatures.body: At $3,598 in October 2026 the GM Pro 60W MOPA undercuts Monport's split GT 60W MOPA with autofocus by about $670 and the GPro Vision 60W MOPA by about $1,700.

beginnerNotes: This profile is the 60W tier of the GM Pro MOPA, the version to pick when colour and engraving depth both matter. Compare the other tier via the chips.
proTips: For deep relief, use long pulses and high power with several passes, refocusing with the autofocus as the surface goes down; switch to short pulses for the final cleaning pass to brighten the bottom.

editorialDepth.advantages: The GM Pro 60W MOPA is the strongest value in Monport's MOPA range: colour, black marking and deep engraving with autofocus, for well under the price of the split machines.
editorialDepth.limitations: No camera, a 400 mm Z height that limits tall parts, and an open galvo that needs an enclosure or strict eye protection. Specs are Monport's until independent tests arrive.
